summary: Little Space Heroes is an interactive, 2D educational space adventure game designed for 9-year-old children to learn space science and survival engineering through play. Across three missions—the Moon, Mars, and Jupiter—players manage food and water resources while solving real-world NASA engineering challenges, such as testing lunar ice for safe drinking water, building radiation-shielded underground habitats using water and polyethylene, and navigating Jupiter's storms with shape-coded wire puzzles. By replacing scary survival tropes with colorful cartoon art, positive reinforcement, and accessible touch controls, our game translates complex astrophysics and space exploration concepts into an engaging, stress-free STEM learning experience that inspires the next generation of young explorers.
details:
Project Overview & How It Works:
Little Space Heroes (Space Mission Design Game) is an interactive, 2D educational space adventure game designed specifically for 9-year-old children. The game teaches real-world space science, planetary environments, and survival engineering through fun, stress-free gameplay across three levels: The Moon, Mars, and Jupiter.
- Core Survival Mechanics: Players manage Minecraft-style Food and Water bars using limited supplies from a spacecraft fridge, guided by a friendly robot companion.
- Level 1 (The Moon): Children learn lunar facts via interactive cards, explore craters to find ice, and use a Water Test Machine scanner to identify safe drinking water.
- Level 2 (Mars): Players respond to a space radiation alert by digging an underground shelter and shielding it with water tanks and polyethylene panels, learning how these materials absorb cosmic rays.
- Level 3 (Jupiter): Players pilot a vehicle to dodge storms (including the Great Red Spot) and solve an interactive Wire Puzzle to activate the spacecraft's protective radiation shield.

Benefits & Intended Impact:
Complex aerospace concepts—such as In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU), space weather, and radiation shielding—are often too abstract for elementary students. Our game translates real NASA mission challenges into hands-on, curiosity-driven problem-solving. It empowers young learners to think like space engineers while building foundational STEM knowledge without fear of failure.

Tools, Technologies & Software Used:
- Development & Web App: Built as a responsive, touch-friendly 2D web application using HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, and Bolt.dev for rapid prototyping and modular game architecture (allowing easy addition of future planets and missions).
- Design & Presentation: Interactive UI elements, cartoon illustrations, and pitch materials created using digital design tools and Google Drive / PDF documentation.

Creativity & Key Factors Considered by Our Team:
- Child-Friendly & Stress-Free Design: Unlike traditional survival games with scary visuals or harsh "Game Over" screens, our game uses bright cartoon art, cheerful sound effects, positive reinforcement (stars and confetti), and a supportive robot buddy to prevent anxiety.
- Accessibility & Inclusion: We incorporated color-blind-friendly (shape-coded) connectors in the wire puzzle, large touch-friendly buttons, and short, readable text cards tailored for 9-year-olds on mobile and tablet devices.
